title: Submit-path writes are not crash-atomic and their ids are not epoch-scoped
description: Coordinator review 2026-10-19, finding 4: a crash between put_record(effect) and the submissions_used increment (no named checkpoint sits in the window) desynchronizes the counters; after a restart with an advanced clock, the recovery turn re-derives the same proposal_revision and re-puts {work}:effect:{rev}:0 / plan:{work}:{rev} with different created_at -> RecordConflictError loops across restarts. Same family between put_record(outcome) and the completion UPDATE for the fixed id outcome:{work}. The §7 replay comment (fresh records never collide) holds only for epoch-scoped snapshot/envelope ids. Fix shape: fold the submit writes + counter into one transaction or epoch-scope the ids.
close_reason: Fixed with commit on 2026-10-19: submit writes (payloads+effects+plan+submissions_used), terminal writes (admission/reject decisions+outcome:{work}+completion UPDATE), and both intent mints each commit as ONE core transaction; rendering/validation moved to a pure build phase before any write; three DURING_* crash checkpoints name the new windows with restart-recovery regressions (payload rollback asserted, virtual clock advanced across restart so re-derivation cannot ride byte-identical dedup). GLM-flash review applied: 0 critical/high, both mediums (mutation-confirmed test-strength gaps) fixed, bootstrap destination mismatch now a typed error, audit-loss window documented as known. Validation: 342 passed / 0 skipped via 'uv run pytest'; ruff/format/ty clean.

title: Defer/wake cycle does not resume the deferred intent (DEFERRED never returns to OPEN)

title: Episode-scoped context selection needs a designed per-event destination/membership model
description:
GLM-flash review of M2 sections 4+5 found that ContextMemory.eligible_episode_fragments selects the newest core_ingestion rows globally: the episode_ref parameter is unused except as a truthiness gate, and the fixtures' ConversationEpisode grouping only keys work/lease semantics. Cross-episode/cross-room fragments can therefore enter a snapshot and become citable PROPOSE_MEMORY lineage.

Why: fixing it needs a design decision first — where does per-event destination/episode membership live (JournalEntry fields, InboundEvent records created by ingest, or maintained ConversationEpisode.member_event_refs)? None of these exist today.

What: decide the membership model, filter episode selection by the turn's episode, then add a two-episode discrimination test asserting foreign fragments are absent from selected_fragment_refs, coverage input_fragment_refs, and propose_memory's acceptable lineage. Surfaced from the M2 section 4+5 review; not silently patched.
design: Membership model (implements the handoff's specified contracts, no new invention): (1) ingest creates one InboundEvent record per applied journal entry (handoff §4 line 65; REF_TARGETS already declares member_event_refs -> InboundEvent) — the transport row stays normalized per §7, so the enrichment the record needs beyond the row (actor_ref, source_audience_ref, episode binding, optional occurred_at/reply/target/trigger refs) comes from an optional EventPlanner callable passed to ingest by the coordinator/fixture policy; no planner or None binding = no record, fail-closed. (2) The same ingest transaction appends the event ref to ConversationEpisode.member_event_refs (creating a new episode record revision) when the planner binds an episode; idempotent on re-ingest duplicates; episode record missing = skip membership, work still created. (3) eligible_episode_fragments reads the episode at its pinned revision (as-of-turn-start membership), takes the newest MAX_SELECTED_EVENTS member events (append order = journal order), and selects their fragments newest-prioritized within the shared 16 KiB budget — identical budget semantics, episode-scoped instead of global. Fail-closed rules: members confer no scope rights (handoff §5), they only narrow context; unbound events join no episode and are eligible nowhere. M3 runner work wires the RunManifest event policy; the slice's binding source is the ingest caller.
notes: GLM-flash review completed 2026-10-15 after quota reset (0 CRITICAL/HIGH, 2 MEDIUM, 4 LOW, 1 NIT). Both MEDIUMs fixed with regressions: binding is now one idempotent path for applied and replayed-duplicate entries (self-healing when episode/fragment records were seeded late — no permanent non-membership), and an entry citing a fragment with no core record skips enrichment fail-closed instead of raising (cursor never blocked). GAP-recovery rows never bind. Episode revisions go through ref-target verification. LOW 3+6 (same-event revision edits, dormant episode_revision) filed as their own bead.
close_reason: Resolved: membership model implemented per the handoff's specified contracts — ingest creates one InboundEvent per applied entry and appends it to ConversationEpisode.member_event_refs inside the same core transaction (EventPlanner supplies actor/audience/episode enrichment; fail-closed without binding; idempotent on duplicates; episode revisions ref-verified); eligible_episode_fragments reads the pinned episode revision's member fragments within the shared 16 KiB budget instead of global ingestion. Two-episode discrimination test asserts foreign fragments absent from selected refs, coverage inputs, and propose_memory lineage. Design decision recorded in this bead's design field. Full suite 289 passed; ruff/ty clean. Note: the GLM-flash reviewer pass 429'd (shared 5h limit, resets 22:17) — a main-session self-review was done instead (one hardening fix applied: episode revisions now go through ref-target verification); the M3 closure task 2.6 re-runs the GLM review over this code.

title: Revocation cascade through transform-derived views is undesigned
description: GLM-flash review of the l34 revocation implementation (2026-10-17): request_access emits transform-derived MemoryViews (view:{request_id}:transform, constructed INTERNAL_ONLY) with NO dependency edge from the source view, so revoke_view's walk cannot find snapshots that admitted a transform output whose source was withdrawn. Bounded impact today: transform views are internal-only and can never enter an effect-capable snapshot, so no queued effect dispatches through the gap — the exposure is stale internal contexts. Related systemic shape (also pre-existing): build_snapshot persists the snapshot and its dependency edges in separate transactions, so a crash between them leaves a durable snapshot with missing edges the invalidation walks rely on (applies to fragment edges for corrections too). Decide: should revocation cascade through transform chains (view-to-view edges or a recursive walk), and should snapshot+edge writes be one transaction — before any M4+ scenario exercises transform chains or relies on edge completeness for recovery.
close_reason: Both design questions resolved and implemented: (a) revocation cascades through transform chains — the request_access edge (transform output view depends on its granted source, written in the SAME transaction as the record batch) lets revoke_view withdraw the whole chain, stale retained output memories (the scope index stops serving withdrawn data, per I14's 'not just search indices'), and invalidate admitting snapshots, one transaction with the invalidation-job boundary tripped between the cascade and invalidation phases (mid-walk crash with pending writes, rollback pinned); (b) snapshot+edge writes are atomic — build_snapshot persists coverage+snapshot+all edges in ONE transaction via _add_dependency_tx, and check_invariants verifies edge completeness for every current snapshot so any future split-write regression is flagged. Production cascade edge pinned by assertion in test_request_access. GLM-flash review applied: 0 critical/high, all four mediums fixed (batch+edge single tx, non-vacuous crash test, production-edge assertion, retained-memory staleness) plus double-flip dedup, TYPE_NAME parameterization, and naming cleanups. 335 passed / 0 skipped via 'uv run pytest'; ruff/format/ty clean.

title: View revocation does not propagate to snapshot invalidation for queued effects
description: M3 task 1.6 coverage note: dispatch-time revalidation catches an INVALID snapshot (correction path), a superseded authorization, revised policy, revoked capability, changed audience, and edited reaction target — but a MemoryView revoked AFTER the snapshot that admitted it leaves the snapshot ACTIVE, so a queued effect derived through that view is not held. M2 wires view problems at admission time (build-time STALE_CONTEXT) and corrections flip snapshots INVALID post-hoc; revocation-to-snapshot propagation is unwired. Decide before the M3 replay stories if any story exercises revoke-view-after-authorize (story 3 uses target edits, which TARGET_CHANGED covers); otherwise fold the decision into usf.2.
notes: Decision after M3 stories: no acceptance story exercised revoke-view-after-authorize (story 3 uses target edits, covered by TARGET_CHANGED), so nothing blocked. I14 nevertheless names revocation alongside corrections as an invalidation source, so the propagation is contract, not invention — implementing now: a revoke_view API mirroring correct_memory's atomic invalidation walk.
close_reason: Implemented per I14: ContextMemory.revoke_view revokes the view and invalidates every admitting snapshot in ONE core transaction (the invalidation-job checkpoint DURING_CORRECTION_JOB trips inside — crash rolls back and the revocation re-runs, now pinned by a regression), idempotently (stale cite = already revoked; documented why no SUPERSEDED guard). Dispatch-time coverage: a queued effect authorized before revocation holds with STALE_CONTEXT and nothing dispatches (end-to-end regression). GLM-flash review: 0 critical/high; both mediums addressed (crash-rollback claim pinned via the invalidation-job boundary; transform-chain cascade + snapshot/edge transactionality filed as hermes-agora-5e2 rather than silently resolved). 333 passed / 0 skipped via 'uv run pytest'; ruff/format/ty clean.

title: Membership edit semantics undesigned: same-event revisions and episode_revision update rule
description: GLM-flash review of the 93h membership implementation (2026-10-15) surfaced two undesigned edges. (1) Membership dedups by event id only: a same source_event_id arriving at a new source_revision (MESSAGE_UPDATED flow) creates InboundEvent revision N+1 but never updates ConversationEpisode.member_event_refs, which stays pinned at the older revision — selection keeps the originally pinned fragment_refs and nothing flags the divergence. No journal producer bumps source_revision today, so this is latent. (2) ConversationEpisode.episode_revision is a dormant contract field: the handoff (§4.1) lists it with no update rule, membership appends bump only the storage record revision, and nothing reads it. Decide both before M3 replay stories that exercise edits/restarts: whether membership follows event revisions (and what it means for as-of-turn snapshots), and what episode_revision counts.
design: Edit semantics decided (2026-10-16): (1) A same source_event_id at a new source_revision (MESSAGE_UPDATED / MESSAGE_DELETED) is the SAME member event followed at its current revision: ingest writes InboundEvent revision N+1 (the update's journal_seq and fragment refs) and updates the member ref IN PLACE — same conversational position, bumped revision — bumping the episode record revision. Selection still resolves each member at its pinned revision, so a snapshot that pinned the episode before the edit keeps showing the pre-edit content (as-of-turn semantics) while new turns resolve the edited content; a MESSAGE_DELETED is a tombstone member whose empty fragment_refs contribute nothing. The episode record's version history IS the divergence flag. (2) ConversationEpisode.episode_revision stays untouched by membership writes in this slice: the storage record revision is the membership versioning mechanism, and any meaning for the logical field (e.g. room/episode merge detection per I12) gets defined when merges are designed — inventing an update rule now would be presenting an undesigned rule as established.
close_reason: Decided and implemented: same-event revisions follow the member in place (position kept, revision current, episode record revision bumped; as-of-turn snapshots keep the pre-edit view; deletes are tombstones), and episode_revision stays reserved for future merge semantics rather than getting an invented update rule — the storage record revision is the membership version. Design recorded in the bead. Regression: test_membership_follows_event_revisions_in_place (edit followed in place, current vs pinned snapshot divergence, delete tombstone). 292 passed at this state via 'uv run pytest'; ruff/format/ty clean.
